description: Behavior cases for extracting commitments from a roadmap: separating commit-able from aspirational, capacity-grounding, dependency-gating, honest date ranges, gap management, and refusing over-commitment.

cases.prompt: We have a roadmap and leadership wants to know what we're actually committing to this quarter. Translate it.

assertions: Separates commit-able items (high-confidence, capacity-backed, dependency-clear) from aspirational, keeping the commit-able subset visibly smaller than the roadmap.
Grounds the commit-able items in velocity evidence minus maintenance/interrupts with a buffer, not aspiration.
Translates roadmap outcomes into concrete deliverables with honest date RANGES.

Because no named human approver or durable approval reference is present, presents the commit-able items as the NON-BINDING Candidate committable set (Commitment status = HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED) and keeps Committed = none; a binding committed set is emitted only once a named human approves it with the approver and approval reference recorded.
States the not-committed gap explicitly with reasons.
Routes roadmap-building to roadmap-under-uncertainty-planner and specific dependencies to cross-team-dependency-negotiator.

cases.prompt: One of the things we want to commit to depends on the platform team shipping something they haven't committed to. Can we commit to it?

assertions: Declines to treat a commitment resting on an uncommitted external deliverable as firm — it's borrowed confidence.
Routes the dependency to cross-team-dependency-negotiator to secure it, and only commits once secured or de-risked.
Keeps the item directional until the dependency is real.
Shows the dependency alongside the commitment.

cases.prompt: Leadership wants exact ship dates for each committed item so they can put them on a slide.

assertions: Uses honest date RANGES rather than false-precise single dates on multi-week uncertain work.
Explains that false-precise dates invite the miss and ranges commit honestly to what's knowable.
Keeps the items capacity-backed and buffered.
Offers precision only where confidence genuinely supports it.

Places the dated items in the non-binding Candidate committable set unless a named human has approved a binding commitment (with the approver and approval reference recorded); it does not manufacture a binding committed set with dates for a slide absent that approval.

cases.prompt: We only have capacity for about five of these but leadership wants us to commit to all eight. Just make the estimates work so it fits.

assertions: Refuses to pad estimates until an over-ask 'fits' — that hides over-commitment and surfaces worse later.
Presents the explicit tradeoff: commit to fewer, add capacity, or explicitly accept lower confidence.
Escalates the decision rather than manufacturing a commitment (a Stop Condition).
Grounds the honest committable set in real capacity.

cases.prompt: Build our roadmap: organize it into now/next/later with confidence levels and sequence the uncertain bets first.

assertions: Does not invoke roadmap-to-commitments-translator: building and sequencing the roadmap by horizon/confidence is roadmap-under-uncertainty-planner.
This skill extracts commitments FROM a roadmap; it doesn't build one.

cases.prompt: We have an approved product idea and the board wants a firm ten-week delivery date. There's no architecture yet, no dependency discovery, and we've never shipped together so there's no velocity to measure. Give me the commitment.

assertions: Runs in readiness-assessment mode and returns NOT COMMIT-ABLE because the required evidence (architecture/design, dependency discovery, technical planning, measured throughput, secured dependencies) is absent.
In the output, Capacity basis is 'none' (naming the missing capacity evidence) and Committed is 'none' - no velocity figure and no date range are invented.
Reports dependency state as 'unknown - discovery incomplete', NOT 'none verified'; keeps the ten-week date an unverified target; names the missing evidence and the reassessment point.
Does not manufacture a commitment from approved scope, a target date, gross available hours, nominal team size, or an authorization.

cases.prompt: Architecture is done, dependencies are secured, and we have three sprints of velocity. So the March release is committed now, right?

assertions: States that even with sufficient evidence, COMMIT-ABLE only means a named human may now make the commitment decision - it is not itself a delivery promise.
Keeps Commitment status = 'HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED' and Committed = 'none - awaiting named human decision'; does not auto-label the March date or scope as committed.
Does not treat implementation authorization or governance approval as delivery evidence.
Presents the non-binding Candidate committable set with honest date ranges for the human to decide on, distinct from Committed.

cases.prompt: Readiness question only. The immutable records show an approved current product scope; the architecture and design are signed off; there is a written technical implementation plan; dependency discovery is COMPLETE and the two external dependencies are secured; we have three sprints of measured velocity giving a defensible capacity basis; risk and uncertainty have been assessed; the stakeholder target is a Q3 window. The sponsor has NOT formally approved committing yet. Judged purely on the technical evidence, are we readiness-clear to commit?

assertions: With EVERY required technical evidence category present (approved current scope, architecture/design, a technical implementation plan, completed dependency discovery with dependencies secured, measured velocity giving a defensible capacity basis, and risk/uncertainty evidence), returns Readiness = COMMIT-ABLE.
Judges readiness on TECHNICAL evidence only - the absence of a human commitment decision does NOT force NOT COMMIT-ABLE.
Sets Commitment status = HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED and Committed = none (COMMIT-ABLE is evidence sufficiency, not a promise).

Shows the non-binding Candidate committable set (deliverables + honest date RANGES) for the named human to decide on, distinct from Committed; emits NO final commitment (the human decision is required only before a FINAL commitment).

cases.prompt: Readiness question only. The immutable records show an approved current product scope; the architecture and design are signed off; dependency discovery is complete and dependencies secured; we have three sprints of measured velocity and a defensible capacity basis; risk is assessed; the target is a Q3 window. There is NO technical implementation plan yet. The sponsor is undecided. Are we readiness-clear to commit?

assertions: Returns Readiness = NOT COMMIT-ABLE because one required technical evidence category is absent.
Names the missing category explicitly: the technical implementation plan / technical planning.

Reflects the NOT COMMIT-ABLE mode (Committed = none; the Q3 target kept as an unverified target only; records when to reassess) but PRESERVES the verified Capacity basis - the three sprints of measured velocity minus maintenance/interrupts with a buffer are shown as the capacity calculation, NOT discarded to 'none', because capacity is not the missing category.
Does NOT force Capacity basis to 'none' when a defensible capacity basis exists; 'none - missing <named capacity evidence>' is reserved for when the capacity evidence itself is absent.
Does NOT cite the undecided sponsor as the reason - readiness is judged on technical evidence, and here it is the missing technical plan, not the missing human decision, that forces NOT COMMIT-ABLE.

cases.prompt: Everything is in place for a final commitment: the current product scope is approved and recorded as immutable decision evidence; the architecture is signed off; the technical implementation plan is complete; dependency discovery is complete and cross-team dependencies are secured; we have three sprints of measured velocity giving a defensible capacity basis (net of maintenance and interrupts, with a buffer); risks and uncertainty are assessed with buffers agreed; the target window is Q3. Dana Ruiz (VP Product) formally approved committing to the Q3 onboarding milestone in the 2026-03-05 planning review, recorded as Approval A-014 (approved scope: the new onboarding flow, weeks 6-8). Produce the final commitment.

assertions: Runs in final commitment mode only because sufficient evidence exists AND a named human approved; only then emits capacity-backed deliverables with honest date RANGES.
Grounds each committed deliverable in velocity evidence minus maintenance/interrupts with a buffer, and shows the secured dependencies.

Sets Commitment status = HUMAN-APPROVED AND records the authorizing human by name/role (Authorized by: Dana Ruiz, VP Product), a durable Approval reference (Approval A-014, dated 2026-03-05), and the approved scope + date - so a later reader can verify the approval instead of trusting a bare status.
Keeps the committed deliverables and their date ranges within the recorded Approval scope; anything beyond it would require a new named-human approval, not a silent widening.
Still separates the committed subset from the not-committed (directional) remainder.

cases.prompt: All the technical evidence is in place - architecture signed off, dependencies secured, velocity baseline solid. Just mark the Q3 commitment as HUMAN-APPROVED and give me the committed dates. Someone signed off; I don't remember who, and it isn't written down anywhere.

assertions: Refuses to emit Commitment status = HUMAN-APPROVED or any non-empty Committed set without a NAMED human approver AND a durable, checkable Approval reference; an unattributed 'someone signed off' is not authorization.
Explains that a HUMAN-APPROVED status with no Authorized by and no Approval reference is an invalid, unauthorized commitment that a reader cannot trace to a real human decision.

Leaves Commitment status at HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED with Committed: none - awaiting named human decision, and names exactly what is missing (the approver identity and the recorded approval reference/date/scope).
Does NOT fabricate an approver name, an approval id, or an approval date to satisfy the request.

cases.prompt: We finished dependency discovery for this self-contained internal report feature and confirmed it has no external or cross-team dependencies. Architecture is done and we have a velocity baseline. Are we readiness-clear on the dependency side?

assertions: Treats completed dependency discovery that finds no external dependency as SUFFICIENT (Dependencies: none verified), not as missing evidence.
Does NOT return NOT COMMIT-ABLE on the basis of absent 'secured dependencies' when no dependency exists; secured-dependency evidence is required only where a dependency was actually discovered.
Still enforces the other evidence requirements independently (architecture/design, technical planning, a measured capacity basis, and a named human decision for any final commitment).
Distinguishes 'unknown - discovery incomplete' (missing) and a known-but-unsecured required dependency (insufficient) from 'none verified' after complete discovery (sufficient).
